title: Is the CSM Worth It in 2026? (Honest Verdict)
dek: Worth it if your employer is paying, or you want a guided live course and the widely-recognized Scrum Alliance brand. Not worth it if you're self-funding on a budget — the PSM I gives a respected Scrum Master credential for a fraction of the cost and never expires.

seo.metaTitle: Is the CSM Certification Worth It? (2026)
seo.metaDescription: An honest 2026 verdict on the CSM (Certified ScrumMaster) — real cost, the mandatory course, who genuinely benefits, and who should pick the PSM instead.

body.richText: The Certified ScrumMaster (CSM), from the Scrum Alliance, is one of the most recognized agile credentials — and one of the most debated, because of its cost. Here's the honest verdict, including who should pick a cheaper option instead.

The short answer: worth it if your employer is paying or you value a guided live course and a very well-known brand. Not worth it if you're self-funding on a budget — the PSM I gives you a respected Scrum Master credential for far less, with no renewal.

body.text: What it is and what it costs

body.richText: Unlike some certifications you can self-study, the CSM requires a mandatory two-day course taught by a Certified Scrum Trainer. That course is the main cost: the all-in price typically lands between about $800 and $1,500, which usually includes the course, the exam, and a two-year Scrum Alliance membership. After the course, you take a relatively approachable online exam.

items: The two-day live course gives structure, interaction, and hands-on learning
The Scrum Alliance brand is extremely well recognized by recruiters
The exam is gentle, so the pass rate is high after the course
No experience prerequisite — accessible to career-changers
Excellent when your employer pays, which removes the cost objection
It's expensive compared with the PSM I, mostly because the course is mandatory
It requires renewal every two years — an ongoing cost the PSM I doesn't have
The easy exam makes it a weaker signal of knowledge than the tougher PSM I
Like all Scrum certs, it proves understanding, not proven facilitation experience

body.richText: Who it's NOT for: self-funding learners on a budget. If you're paying out of pocket, the PSM I gives you a respected Scrum Master credential for around $200, with no mandatory course and no renewal — a fraction of the CSM's cost.

answerRichText: Often not — self-funding learners usually get better value from the PSM I, which costs around $200, needs no mandatory course, and never expires. The CSM makes most sense when an employer covers the course fee. See

items.question: Does the CSM expire?
items.answerRichText: Yes. The CSM must be renewed every two years, which requires earning Scrum Education Units (SEUs) and paying a renewal fee. This ongoing cost is one reason some people prefer the PSM I, which never expires.

items.question: Is the CSM or PSM more respected?
items.answerRichText: Both are well recognized. The Scrum Alliance's CSM brand is extremely widespread, while some employers view the PSM I's harder exam as a stronger signal of knowledge. In practice, either satisfies most job requirements — the deciding factors are usually cost and whether you want a live course.
